steps.npc: Hello! What can I do for you today?
I'm Marwolaeth, bringer of prophecy.

steps.player: It's nice to meet you Marwolaeth, I'm [player name].

steps.npc: And it's great to meet you, [player name].
I'm the local wisdom, my dreams are those of prophecy. Would you care for a reading?

options.text: Yes, tell me of my future...

steps.player: Yes, tell me of my future...

steps.text: If wearing an item aligned to Saradomin:

steps.npc: I see a blinding light! A fire so big the heavens can see it; all those who look upon the great flame struggle to look away.

steps.text: If wearing an item aligned to Zamorak:

steps.npc: I see a darkness so thick, light fails to escape it - A shadow world where up is down and right is wrong.

steps.text: If wearing nothing/items aligned to neither:

steps.npc: I see peace and prosperity - The air is filled with wonderous bird song and the scent of earth and river.
It isn't my place to derive meaning. Allow my foretelling to guide your future but do not rely upon it happening all by itself. We are the arbiters of our own destiny.

steps.player: That's really quite vague, do you just say this to everyone?

steps.npc: It's your choice to believe, not mine.
You're most welcome, [player name].
Was there anything else you wanted?
Are you sure?

steps.player: I'd prefer to stay ignorant... Who knows what that knowledge could do to a person...

steps.npc: A blissful existence may be the correct path.
Was there anything else you wanted?

options.text: Can you tell me about this place?

steps.player: Can you tell me about this place?

steps.npc: I can! This is the quaint town of Gwenith. All those who have been granted access to the great crystal city of Prifddinas are welcome here.
Ah... It is expected for an outsider like yourself to notice the mountain wonder how we exist in its shadow.
We leave the mountain alone and it lets us live peacefully, out of sight of any passing boats.
Of course! At the very top of the mountain sits a ruin. Whatever calamity happened there; their ghosts remain.
Yes. Explore at your own peril, [player name]. There are those who have looked for answers from these mynydd spirits. They never return.

steps.player: That doesn't necessarily mean they died... They may have found the meaning that they desired and have gone elsewhere.

steps.npc: Elsewhere? Indeed... As I said, [player name], explore at your own peril. Was there anything else you wanted?
Farewell, adventurer.
